content:
Robotics hardware startup coprod has raised $6 million in a pre-seed
funding round led by Founderful and PROTOTYPE, with participation from General
Catalyst, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures,
SDAC, Unruly Capital and Venturekick. The round also attracted angel investors,
including Hugging Face founder Thomas Wolf, the Dassault family and Florent
Perrichon.

Founded in late 2024 by graduates of the École polytechnique fédérale de
Lausanne (EPFL), coprod develops compatible hardware components for robotics
and physical AI applications, aiming to reduce the time, cost and complexity of
building specialised robotic systems.

Developing robots with custom hardware typically requires significant
investment, specialised engineering teams and several years of development. One
of the main challenges is integrating components from different suppliers,
which often use incompatible systems and require extensive custom electronics
and software work.

coprod aims to simplify this process through an ecosystem of compatible
hardware components, called "co:products", supported by a software
API and configuration tool. The platform standardises communication between
components while maintaining the real-time performance needed for reliable
robotic systems.

According to the company, its approach could reduce development timelines
from two to three years to a few months, allowing smaller teams to build and
test robotic platforms at an estimated cost of $5,000 to $25,000 per design
iteration.

The founders initially demonstrated their approach by building a bipedal
robot in a garage in the Swiss Alps. Since then, coprod's components have been
integrated into several robotic projects in Switzerland, including the first
student-built Swiss humanoid robot developed by the ETH Robotics Club, which
recently took its first steps in Zurich.

Loïc Delineau, CEO and co-founder of coprod, said that simplifying
hardware development will make robotics more accessible and encourage wider
adoption of purpose-built systems:

We believe that a robot with purpose-built hardware designed for a
specific task will do that task faster, cheaper and more reliably than any
general purpose robot ever could, regardless of which model runs on it.

By the end of 2027, coprod plans to have its complete component range
commercially available, qualified, certified and packaged. Large-scale
production is expected to take place in Shenzhen and Texas, while the company's
headquarters, core team and research and development operations will remain in
Switzerland.

The new funding will support the commercial launch of coprod's first
hardware components and the development of a prototyping facility in Lausanne.
Equipped with CNC machinery, lasers and electronic assembly and testing
equipment, the facility is expected to reduce development cycles from two weeks
to 24 hours.

It will also enable the company to provide detailed technical
documentation and digital twin models for its components, helping improve the
transition from simulation to real-world robotic applications.
